name: Archaeological Sites of the Island of Meroe
description: In the semi-desert of northern Sudan, between the Nile and Atbara rivers, Meroe was the royal city of the Kingdom of Kush, which ruled for roughly a thousand years. Over two hundred steep-sided pyramids, many now ruined, rise from the sand in three groups. Nearby, the temples of Naqa and Musawwarat es-Sufra show how Egyptian and African traditions blended in Kushite art and architecture.
